newsitem.title: USA: Telxon says to close Toronto facility.
newsitem.headline: Telxon says to close Toronto facility.

text.p: Telxon Corp said on Friday that it had begun closing its Toronto facility as part of a centralization plan to generate roughly $10 million in annual savings.
The plan involves moving the Toronto operations of the company's Aironet Wireless Communications Inc unit into Telxon's Akron-based headquarters.

In a statement, Telxon also said it plans to consolidate some of its product development and customer support operations to Houston, Texas, in close proximity to its existing manufacturing and National Service Center operations.

"We believe that once the two-year implementation of these initiatives is complete, the efficiency improvements and overall cost reductions that result will generate about $10 million in annual savings," said Telxon chief financial officer Kenneth Haver.
He added that the relocations are expected to occur over the next 12 to 18 months and to reduce current North American employment by 40.
"We expect that the transition plans will have no material impact on the company's targeted operating earnings for fiscal 1998 or our near-term quarterly performance," Haver said.
Aironet, a Telxon subsidiary, is a designer and manufacturer of wireless LAN products. Telxon makes and services portable, battery-powered computers.
